# TinyDoc

> TinyDoc is an open-source Python engine that turns receipt and invoice images into schema-validated JSON with exact OCR-span evidence and per-field confidence. It runs local Qwen2.5-VL-3B or Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct models through Ollama. It is not a TinyDoc-trained checkpoint.

## Key facts

- Package: `pip install tinydoc` (0.3.0), Apache 2.0, Python 3.9+.
- Readers: `qwen2.5vl:3b` (quality) and `qwen3-vl:2b-instruct` (fast); both Apache 2.0.
- Output: JSON Schema-valid fields, per-field quote/page/bbox evidence, confidence, optional overlay PNG.
- Runtime: local Ollama. No API key, no cloud, no telemetry.
- Receipts: 0.9475 field F1 (3B) and 0.9200 (2B) on SROIE clean-100 — public train split, duplicate-filtered, not an external benchmark; 60% of the original set is leaked.
- Invoices: 91.9% key-header / 65.7% fully correct (3B) and 93.5% / 71.8% (2B) on a synthetic 181-document, page-1-only benchmark. Not real supplier invoices.
- Multipage: on 10 synthetic invoices (46 pages), all-pages gets 4/10 fully correct and 71.1% key-header, with two 8-page runaway failures; page-wise VLM gets 6/10 fully correct, 93.3% key-header, and 0.848 line-item F1, with zero parse errors. Adding deterministic reconciliation (last-page currency, arithmetic repairs, OCR-read printed totals accepted only when subtotal + tax == total) reaches 10/10 on the nine key-header fields, with an exact 95% CI of 69.2-100% at n=10. That is a pipeline result, not a pure VLM score; line-item F1 is 0.848, all lines are right on 1/10, page-wise is about 2x slower (70.7 s/doc p50, 16.1 s/page). A deterministic degraded copy of the same 46 pages completed 8/10 documents: 7/8 fully correct, 71/72 key-header (98.6%), 0.795 line F1, OCR consistent on all 10 final pages, and 2 page failures (one malformed JSON, one transient Ollama HTTP 500). The 0.3.0 SDK preview exposes the page-wise path; that is probe-quality, not a production multipage claim.
- Real Portuguese probe: 100 real phone photos of receipts/simplified invoices (80 company, 20 personal), CC BY 4.0, human labels for five fields. Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct at 1400 px scores 74.2% field accuracy (428/577) and 18/100 fully correct with an unreleased preserve-printed-total merge fix; the shipped 0.3.0 merge scores 64.8% and 3/100 because it double-counts VAT on tax-inclusive receipts. Development set; the seed-43 holdout is frozen but not run; not a B2B supplier-invoice benchmark.
- DocVQA reading probe: 200 public images, one question per image, 768 px mirror, single reference. Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct scores 0.829 ANLS and 0.765 exact match, 0 errors, 3.36 s p50. Not comparable to DocVQA leaderboard numbers; the set may be in pretraining.
- Evidence coverage: 0.798 of non-empty fields. Grounding is OCR spans; VLM-predicted boxes failed the 0.70 gate (hit@0.5 0.04–0.20).
- Confidence: field-level ECE 0.115–0.135 raw, 0.005–0.014 after document-grouped isotonic out-of-fold. Document-level confidence is not calibrated. Use for review routing, not as a probability.
- Not measured: real B2B supplier invoices, the seed-43 real-document holdout, real-document line items/flags/confidence. Flagging fails (0/7). The multipage probe is not a production claim, and DocVQA is a single-reference reading probe.

## Short answers

- What is TinyDoc? A local-first extraction SDK and CLI for receipts and invoices, with cited output.
- Does it ship a model? No. It uses third-party Qwen VLMs and adds the extraction and trust layer.
- Does it need the cloud? No. Inference runs on a local Ollama server.
- Is it production-ready? It is a developer preview. Real B2B supplier invoices are unmeasured; a 100-document Portuguese receipt/invoice probe is measured on five fields (development set, 74.2% field / 18/100 fully correct with an unreleased merge fix). Multipage is a 10-document probe (page-wise VLM 6/10; 10/10 key-header only with deterministic OCR reconciliation, ~2x slower), and flagging fails.
- Is the confidence a probability? No. Field scores are for review routing; document scores are not calibrated.
- Does it predict boxes? It returns OCR-span boxes as provenance. Model-predicted boxes did not meet the gate.
- Does it handle multipage invoices? The eval harness can send every page or read page-wise: all-pages 4/10 fully correct, page-wise VLM 6/10 and 93.3% key-header on 10 synthetic documents. Deterministic reconciliation plus OCR totals reaches 10/10 key-header, but that is a pipeline result, not a pure VLM score; line items remain weak. A degraded copy completed 8/10 documents with 7/8 fully correct and 2 page failures. Page-wise is about 2x slower; the 0.3.0 SDK preview exposes the page-wise path, but it is probe-quality.
- How accurate is it? 0.9475 receipt F1 (3B) on SROIE clean-100; 91.9%/65.7% invoice key-header/fully-correct (3B) on a synthetic page-1 probe; 74.2% field / 18/100 fully correct (2B, unreleased merge fix) on 100 real Portuguese receipts/invoices, five fields, development set.
- How well does it read documents? On 200 public DocVQA images with one reference answer, 0.829 ANLS and 0.765 exact match (2B); a reading probe, not a leaderboard score.
- What is planned? Validate the merge fix on the frozen seed-43 real-document holdout, test a receipt-aware/header-first prompt, then chunked page-wise latency work, a dedicated calibration split, and real B2B supplier-invoice evaluation. The preview already ships page-wise merge and OCR total reconciliation locally via `tinydoc ui` and `tinydoc invoice`.
